The page gives the nonuniqueness force as “$F(x)=m\sqrt{|x_{1}|}\,e_{1}$” for a unit-mass model. Under `def-cm01-units`, mass has dimension $\mu$ and position has dimension $\ell$, so this expression has dimension $\mu\ell^{1/2}$, not force dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. The current counterexample item instead uses $\lambda\sqrt{|x_1|/\ell_*}$ and declares the dimensions of $\lambda$ and $\ell_*$. Confirmed independently against exact current unit/flow/continuation suppliers; local corrected carrier now removes this observed defect, with repair described in report.

The setup specifies $N$ labels, $Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$, and $\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^3$, then claims the model motion is $x(t)=x_0+v_0t+\tfrac12\mathbf g t^2$. `def-cm02-newtonian-flow` defines a motion as $x:J\to Q$ and initial data with $x_0\in Q$, $v_0\in(\mathbb R^3)^N$. Thus for $N>1$ the displayed sum is not typed: a single 3-vector cannot be added to the full configuration. The item does not set $N=1$ here or define the repeated tuple of field vectors. The title claims “finite-time breakdown requires escape from every compact subset of the state domain.” But Statement clause 2 concerns compact subsets of $D=I_0\times U$, while clause 4 requires $I_0=\mathbb R$ before concluding state escape. For a counterexample, take $I_0=(0,1)$, $Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$, $F\equiv0$, and zero initial velocity. The constant state has maximal interval $(0,1)$ and remains in a compact singleton of $U$ as its finite right endpoint is reached. Only the time-state graph leaves compact subsets of $D$.
